page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance includes a dedicated NVIDIA Pascal P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. It does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps under the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the CPU and memory subsystems operate in lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, while the multi-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, PassMark CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests are in the bottom 25%, though the overall PassMark CPU score reaches the middle 50%.

The absence of local storage and the 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth represent notable architectural constraints for data-intensive operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA P4 GPU provides hardware acceleration capabilities for workloads that do not require high-performance host CPU processing or massive memory bandwidth. This server is suited for entry-level GPU-accelerated tasks, basic machine learning inference, video transcoding, and legacy CUDA applications that can tolerate lower CPU and memory throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated server featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 CPU cores, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA Pascal P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, this instance lacks local storage and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows weak CPU and memory performance, with stress-ng multi-core and memory bandwidth results falling into the bottom 25%, and single-core CPU performance in the bottom 10%. The PassMark CPU score sits in the middle 50%. Given these performance characteristics and the dedicated GPU, this server is positioned for entry-level GPU workloads, basic machine learning inference, and video transcoding where host CPU and memory throughput are not primary bottlenecks.
